title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio with José Manuel Acevedo of RCN
text: hide Secretary of State Marco Rubio with José Manuel Acevedo of RCN Interview Marco Rubio, Secretary of State September 8, 2026 Via Teleconference September 9, 2026 (Via translation.) QUESTION: Well, it is a tremendous honor to have with us here at RCN and NTN24 the United States Secretary of State, Marco Rubio. Secretary, thank you for being here with us. SECRETARY RUBIO: No, thanks. It’s a great honor to be with you as well. QUESTION: They are also watching us in Miami and throughout Latin America thanks to NTN24. As you know, we are networks that have followed your work closely since you were a senator and now as Secretary of State. And now you come to a country like Colombia, one that is not unfamiliar to you, because it must be said that you have defended democracy in our country, Colombia. Additionally, if you’ll allow me a personal question, your wife also has very deep roots in this country. What is your personal connection to Colombia? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, my wife—her mother was born in [inaudible], stayed in [inaudible], and then moved to Bogotá. She still has relatives here. And I live in Miami, and I don’t know if you know this, but there are a lot of Colombians in Miami. QUESTION: Lots of them. SECRETARY RUBIO: And that’s why I wanted to mention it. And in Broward as well. But I have always followed Colombia very closely for two reasons. The personal connection is always important, and we follow everything that happens in the country very closely because of that relationship, but also because of the relationship between our two countries. You have to understand that for more than 20 years, throughout my entire time in the Senate, for example, the most important partner we had in South America was Colombia, the most consistent one. There were changes of government in different places, but when it came to economic and security matters, the most important partner the United States had was Colombia. That was broken over the last four years. Unfortunately, although many relationships still existed at the military and security levels and so forth, we went through a period that, I would say, was not natural in our relationship. It was somewhat damaged, unfortunately. But now we are entering a new stage, and I believe we are quickly going to recover what we had—and not simply recover what we had. We are going to be able to expand it even further, because you have a president here who has tremendous enthusiasm, a lot of energy, a lot of vision, and who is willing to take risks, but who is also responsible and knows the American system well. He understands well how our system works. That is also going to help him greatly in building that connection. QUESTION: In fact, I remember you saying, “The best days are yet to come for Colombia,” after your meeting with Abelardo de la Espriella, and I imagine you still feel the same way. But for that to happen, we need cooperation, especially on an issue that I know has long been a concern for both you and the President: security. How do you view the security situation in Colombia? SECRETARY RUBIO: I have said it, and I will continue to say it. The most important responsibility of any government, at any level—municipal, departmental, state, as we say in the United States, or at the federal or national level—is security. It is the most important thing the government does: security. The security of a country, the security of a community, the security, the security of its people, and that is the most important thing. And to a certain extent, I think that was somewhat neglected in the thinking of the previous government over the last three or four years. You have a president who was very clearly elected, who made it very clear during his campaign and has made it clear now as president that his number one priority is to restore stability and security for the Colombian people, and we are going to help in every way possible. On top of that foundation of security comes prosperity. Prosperity is impossible without security. It is impossible to invest in a country that is unsafe. It is impossible to invest in a country that is dominated by cartels or criminal gangs. In many cases, these are not just Colombian criminal gangs; they are transnational, operating in Ecuador, Mexico, and other countries in the region. So, for us, security is fundamental. It is the most fundamental thing a government does, and these threats affect us as well, so we are going to help in every way possible. But it is not just about security; it is about security and prosperity. The two go together. QUESTION: Look, Secretary, we are being attacked with drones by illegal armed groups, and in that regard, support with technology and upgrading equipment that is already obsolete in Colombia is very important. But there is another issue that is also of great concern, and that is the attacks coming from the other side of the border. You know that Venezuela has granted impunity to many of those criminals. What can the United States do on both fronts? Technological and Venezuela. And the criminals? SECRETARY RUBIO: Let’s talk first about the situation in Venezuela. We have the ELN and the president of the FARC operating openly and with impunity from Venezuelan territory. This has been going on for more than 10, 15 years. That has to be resolved. We have made that clear to the interim authorities in Venezuela, and I think that is going to be key to improving relations between the two countries. It is impossible for relations to truly improve while that issue remains as it is. No country can allow criminal gangs and terrorists to operate with impunity on the other side of its border, attack within its national territory, and then return under the protection of another country’s borders. That cannot be allowed, and we are going to help with that. And we have already spoken with the Venezuelan authorities, including on the issue of drones. The technology is a global threat. This is a global threat because there is a lot of military equipment that requires a government with millions of dollars in order to acquire it. But in the case of these drones, that really is not necessary. Even criminal gangs can possess them and use them to attack and threaten a state. So, one of the things that is needed worldwide, not just in Colombia, is to establish new, modern defenses against this new threat, specifically drones that use fiber optics, which pose an enormous danger because at this time there is no conventional defense against them. So we have already had discussions about that. QUESTION: And is the United States willing to help Colombia? SECRETARY RUBIO: Yes, but we are not only willing to help Colombia; we also need it for our own resources. So, both countries have an interest in developing the new technology necessary to prevent this type of attack and defend against it. QUESTION: Secretary, during the previous administration of President Gustavo Petro, the United States decertified us in the fight against drugs. How close are we to, or how far are we from, being certified again? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, remember that the certification announced this year has to do with the actions that took place last year. We have a completely different view when it comes to the new president and the new administration, this team. So I expect that if they continue to follow through and continue doing what they say they are going to do and what they have already done—I mean, in the last month we have seen more concrete action against these criminal groups than we possibly saw in four years. So I think that if they continue on that path, there is no doubt that the certification will change, as it has in the past. QUESTION: How soon or how far away is that? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, that’s done on an annual basis. It’s possible that it can be done earlier because there’s a waiver process to be able to do it sooner. QUESTION: Are you going to help us in that, I imagine? SECRETARY RUBIO: I, I, what I—I’m going to do everything possible to help Colombia. And obviously, if the new government continues as it already is, it’s not that they’re making promises; they’re already doing it, and they have begun acting against that. I expect that to change. QUESTION: Secretary, there is another issue that is also of great concern to small, large, and medium-sized businesses, and I’m sure it has come up in the conversations you have had over the past month and in the one you had today in Barranquilla. The issue of tariffs on certain products is affecting us. Uh, they are asking for a temporary suspension of some of those tariffs. Are you leaving us with that good news, or are we not there yet? SECRETARY RUBIO: The tariffs, first of all, apply to everyone. They are not specifically directed at Colombia. This is worldwide. The Supreme Court and its ruling against the President’s policy required a change in strategy and the use of a new process, Section 302, which is a U.S. domestic process that is very legal, very, very technical. But the President wants to change that. The way this issue can be resolved is through a bilateral agreement between the two countries, and negotiations on that are underway. I believe there have been two rounds of negotiations, they have progressed very well, and I hope that very soon the issue can be resolved through that agreement between the two countries. And for President Trump, it is a priority. He has said so. He wants to follow through and bring this to a conclusion. He wants to reach a bilateral agreement that eliminates the problem we currently have with the tariffs. QUESTION: Well, that’s good. Hopefully that will be the case. Secretary, I know you are very diplomatic, and you are going to tell me that you cannot say much about the OFAC list and former officials such as President Petro, Armando Benedetti, and others. But tell me, are there any ongoing investigations by the United States into that? SECRETARY RUBIO: It’s not that I’m being diplomatic; I cannot offer opinions or comment on investigations, whether active or not. I cannot comment on that. What I can tell you is that with all these sanctions, in our system there is no sanction that is imposed without evidence, and the evidence is not going to be ignored. If there is evidence that someone has committed a crime, is committing a crime, or has caused harm, that will be pursued. That is not up to me. QUESTION: Are there any active investigations underway? SECRETARY RUBIO: I can’t comment on that because investigations are not under my purview. They are handled by the Department of Justice. So, I cannot comment on whether there are or are not. What I can tell you is that no one ends up on the, on the OFAC list because someone made something up. To be placed on the OFAC list, there have to be facts, there has to be evidence, there have to be concrete things that justify that decision. QUESTION: In the case of these officials. SECRETARY RUBIO: And there may possibly be others who are placed on that list at some point, if there is evidence against them as well. QUESTION: Look, on that note, Gustavo Petro used to say that you had misinformed President Donald Trump. Gustavo Petro is no longer in Colombia; he is no longer the president of Colombia. What does Marco Rubio think of Gustavo Petro? SECRETARY RUBIO: I think he is no longer president, and we are going to deal with the president you have. He is someone I have known for several years, since before he entered politics. I joked earlier that he went crazy and got into politics. But he is someone who was elected by the people of this country and someone we are going to work with. QUESTION: Just so you know, President Abelardo responded, “And you’re next.” SECRETARY RUBIO: Something like that, I think. I didn’t quite understand it; I didn’t see it very clearly, but he—but I had already been in politics for many years. He wasn’t a politician; he had never been a politician. He was interested in politics, but he wasn’t a politician. I knew him as a local businessman in Miami, and then he wanted to contribute to his country, he wanted to help his country. He ran for president when no one thought he was going to win, and he won. And now he is president, and he is the one we are going to deal with. I’m not going to dwell on the past. QUESTION: Look, I know time is short. We’re wrapping up now, Secretary, I promise. But let me ask you about a country that is, close to you, which is Cuba, and also about Nicaragua. What can the United States, and the world, do to finally bring those dictatorships to an end? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, as in every country, first, the primary responsibility for changing a system lies with the people of those countries. That is always the case. Obviously, we do not support what is happening, or what they are doing, in Nicaragua, and we have imposed sanctions against individuals, people who are contributing to the situation that currently exists in Nicaragua. When it comes to Cuba, what we are not going to continue allowing is for a military company called GAESA to keep stealing Cuba’s money, and that is why we have imposed the strongest sanctions in the history of our relationship with Cuba. Tragically, the Cuban people are suffering, but they are not suffering because of us. They are suffering for two reasons. First, because the individuals in charge of that regime are following an economic model that does not work and has never worked. But now it does not work because they have become accustomed, for more than 60 years, to living off assistance from abroad. First, it was the Soviet Union, then it was Hugo Chávez, and when the free oil they were stealing from Venezuela ran out, they were left without oil. That is not our fault. That is their fault for not having a functioning market. And second, because some—many of the leaders in Cuba who are currently part of that regime are incompetent. They do not know how to manage the economy, and they are the ones who have directly contributed to the suffering of the Cuban people. But what we are not going to allow is for them to continue evading sanctions in order to benefit themselves at the expense of the Cuban people. QUESTION: And what do you mean by not allowing it? Carrying out an operation like the one in Venezuela? SECRETARY RUBIO: Not allowing it—well, for example, we are already doing that. We have shut down bank accounts. Many, many foreign companies have left Cuba because of these sanctions, and they have left because those companies were partners, they had entered into business dealings with these elements of the regime, and they were enriching themselves. QUESTION: But could tougher measures be coming, Secretary? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I’m not going to speculate about what those measures might be, but we always have the right to operate and take action to protect the national security of the United States. I’m not going to comment specifically on exactly what can be done, but we have an obligation to protect the national security of the United States if a threat arises in Cuba, Venezuela, or anywhere else in the world. QUESTION: Look, one thing: the possibility of having U.S. military bases in Colombia, yes or no? SECRETARY RUBIO: Anything is possible. Obviously, this has to come through—first, we have to be invited, because this is a sovereign country, and the decision has to be made by the Venezuelan people through—sorry, by the Colombian people, through their elected officials. If they officially make that request to us, then it will be considered to see what is possible. At the end of the day, that decision is up to the President, through the U.S. Department of Defense, the Department of War. But what I can tell you, without a doubt, is that the security relationship between the United States and Colombia is not going to be the same as before; it is going to be better. QUESTION: Look, I’ll wrap up, but as we say here in Colombia, President Abelardo de la Espriella gave me the task to ask you about your political future. The 2028 elections. Am I interviewing one of the strongest candidates for 2028? SECRETARY RUBIO: But I’m not a candidate for anything right now, and I’m 100% focused on my job, and I have to be because I have two jobs. I have my job as Secretary of State, and I also work as the President’s National Security Advisor, so I have plenty of work right now. QUESTION: But is the dream of becoming President of the United States there? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I don’t know what the future holds, but I have no plans at this time. I’m 100% focused on my jobs. QUESTION: Secretary, and speaking of that job, we want to thank you, on behalf of all Colombians, for what you have done for this country and for its democracy. And please, continue to keep in mind cooperation based on equality, trust, and respect between the United States and Colombia. Thank you, Marco Rubio. SECRETARY RUBIO: Thank you very much. title: Secretary Rubio and Colombian President Abelardo De La Espriella at a Strategic Civil Nuclear Cooperation and Critical Minerals Framework Memorandums of Understanding Signing Ceremony
text: hide Secretary Rubio and Colombian President Abelardo De La Espriella at a Strategic Civil Nuclear Cooperation and Critical Minerals Framework Memorandums of Understanding Signing Ceremony Remarks Marco Rubio, Secretary of State Batallon Paraiso Barranquilla, Colombia September 8, 2026 MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Good afternoon. Good afternoon. The Presidency of Colombia and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs would like to welcome you to the – to the ceremony of two memorandums of understanding between the Government of Colombia and the Government of the U.S. of America. We are pleased to have His Highness President Abelardo De La Espriella, who is the president of Colombia, that’s going to be in this act as the witness – as a witness of honor. And we would also like to greet Omar Bula Escobar, who is the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Colombia, and His Excellency Marco Rubio, who is the Secretary of State of the United States of America, who are going to sign both agreements. (In English) Good afternoon. The Presidency of the Republic of Colombia and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs welcome you to the signing ceremony of two memoranda of understanding between the Government of the Republic of Colombia and the Government of the United States of America. We are honored by the presence of His Excellency Abelardo De La Espriella, President of the Republic of Colombia, who joins us as witness of honor. We also welcome His Excellency Omar Bula Escobar, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Colombia, and the Honorable Marco Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States of America, who will sign both instruments. (In Spanish.) (In English) We will now proceed with the signing of the first memorandum of understanding, the Framework Between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of Colombia for Securing of Supply in the Mining and Processing of Critical Minerals and Rare Earths. (Applause.) (The Memorandum is signed.) (Applause.) (Via interpreter) Okay, thank you so much. We will now proceed with the signing of the second memorandum of understanding that it’s called the Memorandum of Understanding Between the Government of Colombia and the United States of America about Civil Strategic Cooperation, signed by the chancellor of Colombia and the Secretary of State of the U.S. (In English) We will now proceed with the signing of the second memorandum of understanding, the Memorandum of Understanding Between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of Colombia Concerning Strategic Civil Nuclear Cooperation. (Applause.) (The Memorandum is signed.) (Applause.) (Via interpreter) Thank you so much. Thank you so much. And now we were going to go to the joint declaration about the meeting between the – the statement between Abelardo De La Espriella and the Secretary of State of the United States Marco Rubio. And we’re going to initiate with the Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Mr. Secretary, welcome. Welcome. SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Thank you so much, Mr. President. And thank you. I’m so glad – I’m so glad. I came here last time as a senator but in the last four years as a senator, and then as the Secretary of State we hadn’t traveled here. And I think that until a certain point, this is a signal of the distance that had been created between our governments, which is not natural because the relationship between Colombia and the United States is almost impossible to replicate because they are personal links, cultural links, and also – and also at the economic level. And also we also have the opportunity to restore that natural relationships that we have between our countries, but also to grow into a new stage, a new cooperation stage with our president even stronger than we had before. We talked a lot about security, because always security is key, because without security there is no prosperity. But the opportunities that exist between Colombia and the U.S. is much more than security because it’s the base of everything. Without security it’s impossible to operate as a country and as a society. But beyond that – because sometime people say that I – now they’re telling me I’m speaking in a low – you can hear me well, right? They say I’m speaking in a very low voice. There is no doubt that without security a country cannot progress, and the threats to security that Colombia is facing, it’s the same things that we face in the U.S.: the same networks, the same criminal groups that, although they commit their crimes here, they also commit crimes in the U.S., and they damage our people. But that’s the base. That’s the key. That’s the most relevant thing. And because the most important role of any – of any government in any part of the world, it’s the security of its people. But above that, we can build on prosperity, which is extremely important to move forward. And also the opportunity that exists for Colombia at the economic level are huge, are amazing, and these are opportunities that Mr. President has in mind that we can work together so that it benefits both countries. We have a lot to do because, unfortunately, this government inherited a series of disasters, bad decisions, and we feel – we feel the same when we went into power a year and a half ago. But you are facing the errors of the last four years, and you need to face this. And besides that, there was a disaster. There was an earthquake that was tragical. But there are amazing opportunities, and we’re going to use this opportunity that we have nowadays, because the links between our two governments are so solid to ensure that not only are we going to focus on security, but this is something going to be key in our relationship, but we’re also going to focus in what we call the opportunity of creating a prosperity that helps the North American people and also helps the Colombian people. And this relationship between our governments have a – have direct impact on the daily life of people here but also the people in the U.S., and especially people in the certain part of Florida where I’ve lived most of my life. If you allow, Mr. President, I’m going to give a couple of words. (In English) I want to say a few words in English as well. First, I want to thank the president for receiving us. It – it’s not every day – let me say in this in Spanish first. I should’ve said it earlier. (Via interpreter) It’s not – and we’ve not always traveled to a country and we have the opportunity to exchange with chief of state that you met before they were president, before he was a politician, because of the mutual relationships that we have. And even when we were talking not long ago, the two years ago when we were in the same – we were in the same table at a wedding in the southern part of Florida. That’s why this is a place where the president of the – the president is someone that I’ve met at a personal level. And then he went crazy and decided to become a politician and decided to turn president. (In English) So I think that it’s unusual that you travel to a country that you meet with a head of state and a president who you’ve actually known for years before he was president, before he was even in politics. And as I was joking, when he lost his mind and went into politics, and – but he’s going to do a great job for this country, and I know that. I know that from what I know about him from before he was president. This is a man of energy. This is a man of strength. This is a man of vision and of courage because he’s confronting a very difficult situation. He has inherited many disasters. Obviously, the country faces the aftermath of a natural disaster in an earthquake, but he also faces a disaster that’s institutional, that goes through four years of very bad management and that, frankly, harmed the relationship between the United States and Colombia, something that simply is not natural. The United States and Colombia have a strong bond that exists well beyond just the cooperation of our governments. It’s a strong economic bond. It’s a strong cultural bond. It’s a strong people-to-people bond, a social bond. I can tell you personally, having lived in south Florida the majority of my life, how we follow so closely the events that happen in Colombia, because it has a direct impact on life in south Florida and ultimately in our country. This is the natural state of things, is for the U.S. and Colombia to be strong allies and strong partners, and the last four years is an aberration between our governments. But that is changing as well. Clearly, the most important obligation of any government is to provide for the security of their people. It’s the number one obligation, and that is certainly an issue that you will confront here and that I am confident the president and his team are very serious about, and we’re going to do everything we can to help you. But security is the basic and most important requirement of a government, but prosperity follows closely behind it, and that is opportunity of a country and an economy that provides the opportunity for upward mobility and prosperity for all of its people. And we believe we have a lot we can do together in the field of energy, in the field of trade, in the field of commerce, that allows both countries to benefit: the people of the United States, who I work for, and the people of Colombia, who the president works for and his team works for. So I’m excited that after not having been here for a while, to be back, to be back with someone I know so well as president, who I know has a great vision and energy for the future, and excited to be back in a country that has been our strongest ally and partner in the region for many, many years. And we look forward not just to restoring that but building upon it and creating a golden age of relationships between our two countries and our two people. Muchas gracias . (Applause.) PRESIDENT DE LA ESPRIELLA: Thank you. (Via interpreter) A very special welcome to all of you today. Barranquilla has been the scenario of a – of a very strategic conversation for the present and for the future of Colombia and of our relationship with the United States of America. To welcome the Secretary of State Marco Rubio here in the Colombian Caribbean has a very special meaning, because Barranquilla has been historically the Golden Door of Colombia to the world and represents an absolute conviction of my government because Colombia, it’s not just governed from Bogotá, Colombia; it’s governed from its regions. I would like to thank Secretary Rubio. His presence – we are honored by his presence. He has been an inspiration for this battle for democracy, institutionality, and freedom because there is no Latino in the world that doesn’t feel represented by Marco Rubio, that has always done things the best way possible. And with regards to our community, that’s why I thank you so much, Mr. Secretary of State. It’s a pride and honor to have you here in the land of Barranquilla. I also would like to publicly acknowledge the solidarity of the U.S. Government after the earthquake that we endured on August 10th. They have helped us with 26.5 million U.S. dollars in humanitarian assistance, and besides all of what they are doing regarding the fires that people are suffering near Tolima. No country in the world has helped as much as the United States, and today we’re giving a step forward. We are not going back from the solidarity in the emergency, to a very strategic partnership, a long-term strategic partnership. From this meeting there is a guideline that we’ve called the Barranquilla agreements, and they follow three main topics that are highly relevant for our country and for the hemisphere. We are going to rebuild the homeland, we are going to recover the economy, and we are going to protect the hemisphere. And we’re initiating a historical and close relationship that was interrupted during four years, but it has always been there in the deeper areas, in the deeper basis of Colombia, because the United States has been our partner. We have been their ally and partner, and when the United States and Colombia have worked together, the only thing that we have had, it’s development, security, and progress. The main purpose of this agreement, it’s the rebuilding and the economic recovery. The earthquake left huge challenges in households, in bridges, utilities, and in productive capacity. We were thinking where we wanted to work on cooperation, investment, and funding mechanisms, including the – including the International Development Corporation, other agencies, the private sectors and companies from both countries. We would like to attract investments to the infrastructure, energy, households energy, and the productive reconstruction Colombia is also going to do (inaudible) because we are going to do what we have to do regarding fiscal discipline, the legal certainty, efficiency, expanding better investment conditions. In the same way, I requested Mr. Secretary of State to accompany us before multilateral organisms to enable instruments that allow us to fund these transitions without sacrificing the economic transition of our countries. We are proposing to the U.S. a partnership where Colombia puts project territories, productive capabilities, resources, and clear rules and regulations (inaudible) the U.S. supports investments funding technologies and business capability. Other of the important points, it’s shared prosperity. I have proposed Mr. Secretary to have this bilateral prosperity dialogue with very specific projects with – that has funding, timelines that our teams in Washington are going to continue developing. We identified some policies regarding infrastructure, technology, industry, rebuilding, and also rare – and also rare minerals, which is the treatment we’ve just signed. Colombia has access to two oceans, has the strategic resources and human talent. We need to turn all those opportunities that Colombia has in investments and productive chains, in manufacturing and also in employment for our people. Another very important point, it’s security in the struggle against drug terrorism. Colombia wants to become the first hemispheric security partner with the U.S., and we’re going to be the partner number one in South America. The 21st centuries require new capabilities. That’s why we have proposed to the government, and I said it once again today, the Patriot Plan 21st century is to update airplanes, drones, radars, helicopters, anti-drone systems, aerial defense, mobility, intelligence, cyber defense, special forces, and the maintenance and the operationality. We’re going to have our own resource and we hope to build together capabilities to be able to face sophisticated threats. But at the same time, we need the support – we need the support, a push from the United States, and we’re going to work in a very decisive manner in our fight against drug trafficking. We’re going to start with – we’re going to go through the precursors, we’re going to go through the pathways, we’re going to go through the leaders, we’re going to go to the narc terrorists, we’re going to go through the money laundering and other criminal equity and also those international networks that are a huge challenge not only for the hemisphere but also for humankind. Colombia, it’s ready to have annual quotas, verifiable indicators, and very specific agreements. We’re going to do what we are (inaudible), and with that basis we want to have a co-responsibility that is effective for both countries. Another important thing – it’s the Shield of Americas. We’re already operational. Colombia is going to fulfill its responsibilities. We’re going to have the site in Medellín, and we’re going to do whatever it takes to be able to attack and to be able to give them the place that they deserve, which is either a prison or a tomb. And I say it: If a criminal doesn’t – if a criminal doesn’t follow the law, he is going to – he’s not going to get it his way. And we also talked about Venezuela because we share more than 2,000 kilometers of borders with the neighboring countries, and everything that happens in Venezuela has a direct consequence in Colombia regarding security, migration, smuggling, armed – and armed groups, and also energy. Colombia will participate along with the United States in a very responsible manner in the focused efforts to be able to ensure regional stability and will – and will delve on trans-border cooperation, migration, and security. Our interest, Mr. Secretary of State, it’s that we each have institutionality, stability, and also security. We want to avoid any type of issue. Another very important point that I mentioned to Mr. Secretary, it’s our foreign policy is based on a main policy. It’s that Colombia relates with the world from its own national interests. It has sovereignty, autonomy, pragmatism, and also a long-term vision, and this is where we’re perfectly tuned with the United States. We have now resources, geographic positions, human talent, and also very strategic assets. Our diplomacy needs to turn those strengths in opportunities to be able to become the best partners of the U.S. And we’re going to do it, Mr. Secretary, because this is a new rebirth. Another very important topic, it’s migration and the rule of law. We agreed to delve on migration – more migration cooperation, exchange of information, biometric tools, identifying of the people (inaudible) to struggle against the migrants’ networks, and also the strengthening of border controls. Our idea, it’s that legal migration and – legal, safe, and organized migration, because our principle, it’s the same one that the United States shared. We’re not against migration. We’re against illegal migration, which is something different. And there is a topic that it’s very close to my heart, and I said, Mr. Secretary, you know that many years ago we had – we had a consulate. And I said, hey, as the son of this region, I said if you can please open a consular office in Barranquilla, the alternate capital city of Colombia. And we are – we want a venue. We would like to consider it if possible, Mr. Secretary, because it’s been something that we’ve expected for years. First we had a consular office in Barranquilla, and then they took – and they removed the one from Barranquilla. The idea, it’s to go back to things as were before, and we hope to have here in (inaudible) Barranquilla the American consular office. And once again, a topic that it’s also close to my heart, it’s cooperation to follow the path of the money. We would like to – we would like to see what’s money laundering resources that come from resources and hidden assets, strengthening judicial cooperation and financial cooperation. All of this, it’s going to be under the evidence of the framework of law, due process, and the respect for institutions, because to catch criminals, it’s not enough. We also need to strike the money that supports those financial structures. We need to affect the pocket of the criminals because it will hurt them. This was a very deep, cordial, strategic conversation. Not only are we talking about the United States can do for Colombia, we also talked about what Colombia and the United States can do together for the hemisphere, because Colombia contributes a geographic position, strategic resources, productive capability, human talent, a very experienced armed forces, and a government that is committed. And we would – wanted this – this new stage to start here in Barranquilla, in the Colombian Caribbean, and in the region. The Barranquilla agreements need to turn into projects, investments, and cooperation. In the security and also specific outcomes, we need to rebuild the homeland. We need to recover the economy. We need to protect the hemisphere. As of now, our teams (inaudible) will start to work to turn those expectations, those desires, those projects, and realities. May God bless the United States of America. May God bless Colombia hoy more than ever. (Inaudible.) Thank you. (Applause.) MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Thank you so much, Mr. President. Thank you so much, Mr. Secretary of State. We – in this way, we are fulfilling the agenda of Mr. Marco Rubio to the (inaudible) and city of Barranquilla. Thank you so much. title: U.S. Sanctions VTB Bank for Aiding Iran’s Sanctions Evasion
text: hide U.S. Sanctions VTB Bank for Aiding Iran’s Sanctions Evasion Press Statement Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesman Office of the Spokesman September 14, 2026 The United States sanctioned VTB Bank, one of Russia’s largest financial institutions, for helping Iran evade sanctions and sustain its support for terrorism. VTB Bank opened offices in Iran, built banking ties with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions, and worked to move billions of dollars in Iranian assets. The United States remains steadfast in cutting off the financial lifelines that allow the Iranian regime to fund terrorism, destabilize the region, and threaten U.S. economic security. Today’s action sends a clear message to governments and financial institutions considering similar arrangements: any effort to help Iran evade sanctions will carry serious consequences, including exposure to U.S. financial restrictions. The United States will continue to use every diplomatic and economic tool at its disposal to isolate the Iranian regime. We urge the international community to join this effort to sever the financial lifelines of a regime that threatens peace and security. Today’s action is being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the financial sector of Iran’s economy and advances Operation Economic Outcast—a campaign to completely isolate the regime from the financial lifelines that sustain its malign behavior. Please see the Department of the Treasury’s Press Release . title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Responds to Canada’s Retaliation
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Responds to Canada’s Retaliation The White House September 8, 2026 COUNTERING CANADA’S LATEST RETALIATION AGAINST AMERICAN EXPORTS: Today, to address Canada’s increased discrimination against U.S. commerce, President Donald J. Trump signed five Proclamations pursuant to Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to ban certain products from Canada and modify the scope of the tariffs on certain Canadian products previously announced on July 20, 2026. President Trump is taking decisive and appropriate action to respond to Canada’s additional retaliation and continued discriminatory treatment of crucial American exports. After breaking off trade talks with the United States last month, today Canada imposed new retaliatory tariffs on about $20 billion of U.S. exports, including steel, dairy, and agricultural equipment. Because Canada maintained and in fact increased its discrimination against U.S. commerce with respect to U.S. alcoholic beverages, President Trump, under Section 338, imposed import bans on certain Canadian alcohol and other products that were subject to the 50 percent tariffs imposed under Section 338 in Proclamation 11046. Moreover, because Canada maintained its discrimination against U.S. commerce with respect to dairy, President Trump, under Section 338, imposed import bans on certain Canadian dairy and other products of Canada that were subject to the 50 percent tariffs imposed under Section 338 in Proclamation 11047. To offset the burden to U.S. commerce while better serving the public interest, President Trump is also modifying the July 20, 2026 actions by removing certain products, such as rock salt and cement, from the scope of the Section 338 tariffs and replacing those products with new ones, ranging from all-terrain vehicles (ATVs) to additional dairy products. These Section 338 tariffs apply to all covered goods regardless of whether a good originates under the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) and apply in addition to tariffs imposed under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962. The import bans will take effect on September 29, 2026, and the product additions and removals will take effect on September 15, 2026. PROTECTING AMERICAN WORKERS AND ENSURING FAIR TRADE: President Trump is taking decisive action to address Canada’s additional and continued retaliation and discrimination against U.S. commerce to protect American farmers, manufacturers, and workers. Section 338 empowers the President to exclude products from entering the U.S. market if a foreign country maintains or increases its discriminatory practices. Based on Canada’s most recent escalation against U.S. alcoholic beverages, and continued retaliation and discrimination against U.S. commerce with respect to U.S. dairy and motor vehicles, President Trump has determined that it is necessary and appropriate to ban certain Canadian products from entering the U.S. market. President Trump is also refining the scope of the July 20, 2026, actions to better serve the public interest, and to ensure they continue to effectively offset the burden or disadvantage to U.S. commerce from Canada’s discriminatory measures. The additional Section 338 import bans and tariffs imposed today on certain Canadian products further safeguard American workers from Canada’s discriminatory or unreasonable and unequal practices. CONTINUING AMERICA FIRST TRADE POLICY: President Trump is using all the tools at his disposal to restore reciprocity in our bilateral trade relationships and protect the economic prosperity and national security of the American people. By imposing tariffs to address non-reciprocal foreign trade practices, President Trump is incentivizing companies to reshore jobs and production lines back to American soil. Recent new investments part of over $11 trillion in total investments since President Trump returned to office include: American yogurt maker Chobani is investing $1.2 billion into a production plant in Pennsylvania, with plans to launch a new high-protein milk next summer. British automaker Rolls-Royce completed a $1 billion investment into its Indiana facility that tests and builds engines for the U.S. Air Force. Swiss pharmaceuticals company Octapharma is investing $1.5 billion to establish its first U.S. biopharmaceutical manufacturing facility in South Carolina. In August 2026, for the eighth consecutive month, economic activity in manufacturing continued to expand under President Trump’s leadership, and in July 2026, U.S. manufacturing activity expanded at its fastest pace in over four years. Additionally, the President has directed the U.S. Trade Representative and the Administrator of the General Services Administration (GSA) to remove Canadian-origin products from GSA’s Multiple Award Schedules which manage over $50 billion in federal procurement. While President Trump continues to lock in fair and reciprocal trade deals with nearly twenty trading partners across the globe, Canada continues to retaliate against the United States for its efforts to correct trade imbalances and protect American workers, farmers, and businesses. Over the past year and a half, only two countries have chosen to retaliate against President Trump’s tariffs rather than negotiate a deal with the United States: The People’s Republic of China and Canada. Today’s action reflects President Trump’s continued efforts to defend American workers and ensure fair trade, offsetting the burden and disadvantage on U.S. commerce from Canada’s discriminatory treatment.

title: First Lady Melania Trump’s Personal Vision to Preserve America’s Story Through Superior Design
text: Office of the First Lady First Lady Melania Trump’s Personal Vision to Preserve America’s Story Through Superior Design The White House September 9, 2026 First Lady Melania Trump shared her forward-looking vision on the generational significance of institutional design, declaring that, “The White House stands as an architectural autobiography of America, embodying the enduring values of ambition, democracy, and civic life through its design, craftmanship, and the objects within.” First Lady Melania Trump’s elevated creative vision has played a significant and meaningful role, shaping architecture, landscape, preserving historic interiors, and enhancing decorative arts to carry the White House forward. First Lady Melania Trump’s most substantial design accomplishments include the award-winning design and construction of the White House Tennis Pavilion, the complete renovation of the Queens’ Bedroom and the Queens’ Bathroom, the conservation of the historic Zuber wall covering in the President’s Dining Room; and the 2020 restoration of the Rose Garden, which renewed its historic design while revamping infrastructure and accessibility. The First Lady affirmed that important design “fosters collaboration, conveys dignity, inspires ambition, and creates a sense of belonging to something larger.” First Lady Melania Trump’s White House preservation work also encompassed the East Room floor, State Entrance and Hall marble floors, President’s Elevator, White House Bowling Alley, and Children’s Garden, all demonstrating a broader devotion to American craftsmanship and the preservation of the People’s House. Mrs. Trump highlighted, “Within the walls of the White House, these experiences become essential to our national identity.” Notably, her design work has extended beyond the White House grounds to Camp David, further broadening her approach to preserving and evolving America’s historic presidential spaces. The First Lady exclaimed, “Great design transcends aesthetic appeal; it shapes our lived experiences.” The First Lady’s comments were presented from the White House Rose Garden to honor the 2026 White House Historical Association Presidential Sites Summit. This convening brings together more than 200 leaders from presidential sites nationwide, reflecting on the America 250 celebration, with a view to the future. The full remarks by First Lady Melania Trump are below. The White House: America’s Architectural Autobiography The White House stands as an architectural autobiography of America, embodying the enduring values of ambition, democracy, and civic life through its design, craftsmanship, and the objects within. Generation after generation, America’s ideals and stories are woven directly into the fabric of the White House. Design is a meticulous process that involves a multitude of choices—each line, texture, and play of natural light contributes to an overarching narrative. No detail is too small; what may seem insignificant today can influence how individuals connect with one another and perceive their place in history. Within the walls of the White House, these experiences become essential to our national identity. I encountered this truth firsthand when I sought to uncover the exquisite American War of Independence wallpaper designed by French artist Jean-Julien Deltil and created by the firm Jean Zuber and Co. This wallpaper was hidden behind the walls of the President’s Dining Room in the private Family Quarters. Created in 1852 and initially acquired by the Astor family, this exceptional piece was ultimately concealed beneath a wall treatment. My mission to restore and reveal it was driven by a commitment to preserving a vital piece of our American narrative. The successful unveiling of this work was not merely an act of restoration; it was an investment in the future of our nation’s story. Great design transcends aesthetic appeal; it shapes our lived experiences. It fosters collaboration, conveys dignity, inspires ambition, and creates a sense of belonging to something larger. This philosophy guided my work on the White House Tennis Pavilion, designed in collaboration with the Trust for the National Mall, the Executive Residence, and the National Park Service, and approved by the Committee for the Preservation of the White House, the Commission of Fine Arts, and the National Capital Planning Commission in 2018. Every detail was thoughtfully considered to ensure the new structure harmonized with the historic neoclassical character of the White House Grounds. Completed in 2020, the White House Tennis Pavilion later earned two distinguished architectural awards: the 2025 Palladio Award and the John Russell Pope Award. These honors recognize its design inspiration, which echoes the White House itself through doric columns, fanlight windows, limestone cladding, and a copper roof. The Pavilion exemplifies the power of thoughtful design and serves as a bridge that connects people and generations through shared history. As stewards of the places shaped by those before us, we are tasked with making decisions that honor future generations. It is our duty to ensure that the choices we make today are worthy of the legacy we pass forward. And now, it is my honor to introduce John Rogers, the Chairman of the Board of the White House Historical Association. John is not just a remarkable leader; he is a steadfast ally and supporter, dedicated to preserving the rich heritage of our nation’s most iconic residence. His passion for history and commitment to education inspire all of us to champion the values and stories that shape our democracy. With John’s unwavering support, we are empowered to continue our vital mission and ensure that the legacy of the White House endures for generations to come.

title: United States Department of War and Mongolia's Ministry of Defense Conduct Bilateral Defense Framework
text: On September 8, 2026, Mr. Alvaro Smith, Deputy Assistant Secretary of War (DASW) for China, Taiwan, and Mongolia, led the annual U.S.-Mongolia Bilateral Defense Framework (BDF) with Major General Gankhuyag Davagdorj of Mongolia's Ministry of Defense (MoD). DASW Smith and Major General Gankhuyag identified a structured roadmap for increasing Mongolia's defense spending over the next five years, ensuring that U.S. security cooperation assistance aligns with U.S. interests and Mongolia's defense requirements. They also discussed practical ways to enhance the Mongolian Armed Forces' capabilities and readiness, expand combined military exercises, and strengthen Mongolia's defense industrial base. DASW Smith commended Mongolia for its critical contributions to the Board of Peace and Haiti Gang Suppression Force. He emphasized that Mongolia's Strategic Third Neighbor Partnership with the United States remains vital to the defense relationship.

title: Remarks by Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby at the Ukraine Defense Contact Group (As Delivered via Video Teleconference)
text: Minister Pistorius and Secretary Streeting — thank you for convening this important session once again. I send my regards on behalf of Secretary Hegseth to Secretary General Rutte and the distinguished Ministers and officials assembled for this forum today. At our last UDCG, I spoke about the significant transition underway: European allies assuming the leading role providing for their conventional defense and, additionally, the bulk of support for Ukraine. This transition is no longer merely a concept. It is taking hold, and it is producing tangible results. This progress has been directly supported with uninterrupted deliveries of European-funded U.S.-origin weaponry through the PURL initiative. In recent months, Ukrainian forces have sustained a stout defense — holding the front line and denying further Russian advances, while continuing to defend against aerial attacks. This provides an important lesson. Europe's greater assumption of responsibility for its own defense is fully consistent with a strong and viable Ukrainian defense — provided that Europe continues to act with requisite seriousness and urgency. In particular, the denial defense approach that forms the core of our military strategy for Europe has proven effective. Ukraine's ability to deny Russia the gains it seeks is not only critical to Ukraine's self-defense and to the prospects for a lasting peace; it is also an important example for Europe of how combat-credible conventional defense can deny territorial gains. We should, however, be clear-eyed about the outlook. As President Trump has stated, our goal is a lasting peace. We are supporting every effort in that direction. From the standpoint of the Department of War, however, we cannot predict when this tragic war will end. As you all well know, Russia is reconstituting its forces and defense-industrial capacity. We must be prepared for a protracted conflict and for Ukraine's requirements to persist in the months and years ahead. And we must also be prepared for other plausible contingencies as well. That reality makes it all the more important for Europe to sustain support for Ukraine while also accelerating its own rearmament and reindustrialization. Fortunately, this is happening— but we must not be complacent. First, Europe must continue — and where necessary increase — support for Ukraine's immediate battlefield requirements through PURL. The continued flow of munitions and critical capabilities is effective; it remains essential to enabling Ukrainian forces to hold the front line and deny further Russian advances. Second, Europe must plan now for sustained procurement that supports both Ukraine's long-term force reconstitution and Europe's own defense requirements. As allies, we must ensure that needed European investment in its defense industrial base are integrated with and complementary to America's. We welcome greater European investment into your own defense industrial bases. We recognize that is natural and practical. But I stress that we must plan for and implement our investments based on military efficacy, not ancillary objectives. In this vein, support for Ukraine contributes to Europe's security by helping to rebuild Europe's military strength and industrial capacity. But words are not enough. Real money and industrial capacity must be put to work. Again, I underline that this is happening but we must not slacken. The United States stands ready to continue supporting this effort. Through JUMPSTART, we are enabling allies and partners to procure exquisite capabilities for Ukraine, including air-defense interceptors. In Ankara earlier this year, NATO allies committed to supporting Ukraine on an equitable, predictable, and sustainable footing. Now those commitments must be translated into sustained action: Resourcing Ukraine's defense, expanding production capacity, and building the forces and industrial base Europe will need for the generation ahead. These actions demonstrate what an ally-led defense looks like in practice, strengthening the credible deterrence that we are all pursuing as NATO 3.0. We are confident that our allies can and will lead in supporting Ukraine's self-defense, and that this endeavor is highly correlated with Ukraine's own battlefield success. Europe has shown what it is capable of achieving . Just recently, as I visited NATO Headquarters as well as SHAPE Headquarters last month, I saw further evidence that allies are functionally unanimous in NATO 3.0 as a strategic approach and the viability and promise of a Europe-led defense of the continent. This is at the heart of the ongoing Force Posture Review, announced by Secretary Hegseth earlier this year at NATO. In the spirit of flexible realism and strategic rigor, we are advancing and accelerating NATO 3.0 to adapt America's strategic posture in Europe and transition to a more durable and powerful European-led conventional defense. We are moving together in the right direction, thanks to President Trump and key European leaders like Secretary General Rutte. Now is the time to double down on that momentum to build a Europe with the strength and ability to lead on collective defense for the Continent. Thank you very much.

title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Supports America’s Ranchers
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Supports America’s Ranchers The White House September 4, 2026 DEFENDING AND STRENGTHENING OUR NATION’S VITAL RANCHING INDUSTRY: Today, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order launching a whole-of-government effort to protect and fully support America’s ranchers. The Order tasks a comprehensive review and upgrade of all federal government agency regulations and policy to promote ranchers’ interests, directing the Secretary of the Interior, U.S. Trade Representative, Commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration, and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration to assess all regulations, guidance, and any other policy affecting ranchers and prepare further actions to promote ranchers’ financial viability and market access. The Order directs the Secretary of the Interior to determine whether gray wolves or Mexican wolves meet the criteria for delisting or downlisting under the Endangered Species Act (ESA) and begin the process of delisting or downlisting them. The Order further directs the Secretary of the Interior to prepare legislative recommendations for delisting gray wolves and Mexican wolves, and to engage with states to encourage state-level delisting of these species to assist ranchers in combatting predation. The Order directs the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture to update their standards for compensating ranchers for losses due to predators, and to ease authorization for lethal removal when necessary. The Order directs the Secretary of Agriculture to review country-of-origin labeling for beef products. Based on this review, the Secretary of Agriculture may propose new regulations and legislative recommendations regarding such labeling. The Order directs the head of each executive department and agency to ensure that the measures implemented will lower prices for American consumers. EQUIPPING RANCHERS IN MODERN CHALLENGES: President Trump is honoring our hardworking ranchers who feed our Nation by taking decisive action to give them the tools they need to thrive and respond to market disruptions and natural disasters. The President’s immediate action is necessary to protect America’s domestic producers, boost the U.S. supply of beef, and support this critical American industry. The Biden Administration put American agriculture last and delivered one of its most severe beef supply crises in decades, with domestic cattle herds at their lowest level in 75 years. Years of pursuing radical climate activists’ misguided policies and driving up inflation left farmers with historically high input costs and enormous pressure on the ranchers and farmers who feed our country. Additionally, more recent factors have put downward pressure on the size of the U.S. domestic herd, including drought conditions across cattle-producing regions affecting grazing lands and reduced feed and forage availability due to ongoing wildfire conditions. The national herd is at a 75-year low while consumer demand for beef has grown almost 10% over the past decade and is expected to grow even more. Biden-era regulations hindered ranchers’ ability to face nature’s predators, such as gray and Mexican wolves, leaving their herds vulnerable. Burdensome and invasive traceability requirements imposed by the previous Administration unduly hampered small and independent cattle ranchers. From Day One, the Trump Administration has worked around the clock to help rebuild the American beef industry – for the first time since 2018, the number of cattle in the U.S. is increasing and ranchers are retaining heifers at higher rates. FIGHTING FOR OUR RANCHERS: President Trump and his Administration have undertaken an aggressive agenda to reverse Biden’s harmful policies and regulatory burdens, while strengthening the backbone of America’s food supply chain, and ensuring ranchers are prosperous now and into the future. President Trump’s bold America First Trade Agenda has dramatically increased global market access, strengthened farmer and rancher incomes, supported rural jobs, and reduced the agricultural trade deficit. President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts put more money in ranchers’ pockets each year, made the industry more attractive for investment, and boosted profitability for ranchers now and into the future by: Enabling ranchers to depreciate the full value of new business assets in the first year instead of over five years; Allowing ranchers to deduct the full costs of business assets immediately; Making permanent the 20% Small Business Deduction available to family farms and ranchers; Permanently doubling the Death Tax Exemption, letting ranchers pass down their family businesses without massive tax consequences; and, Adding new tax incentives for lenders to make loans for ranchland, reducing ranchers’ borrowing costs. The Department of the Interior and Department of Agriculture have expanded grazing access, ensured millions of acres of public land remain open for grazing, and cut permitting delays on public lands. Since taking office, the Trump Administration has worked tirelessly and successfully to defend the domestic herd from New World Screwworm. Only two active cases in the U.S. remain today, and the Department of Agriculture has expedited the completion of key U.S. sterile fly production facilities. The Department of the Interior initiated measures to mitigate wildfire threats on DOI lands, including using livestock grazing to reduce fine fuel loads. In September 2025, the Internal Revenue Service announced new tax relief for ranchers, allowing them to defer capital gains taxes on livestock or heifers sold due to drought. In October 2025, the Trump Administration announced new actions to fortify the American beef industry, reinforcing and prioritizing the American rancher’s critical role in the national security of the United States. Earlier this week, the Department of Agriculture announced its Ranchers First Initiative , building off of these actions to rebuild the great American beef herd. In December 2025, President Trump signed an Executive Order to stop price fixing, anti-competitive behavior, and foreign influence that drives up grocery prices and threatens the security of America’s food supply. In January 2026, the Department of Agriculture launched its new “Product of USA” label for meat, poultry, and eggs that are born, raised, harvested, and processed all in the United States to ensure marketing protection and benefits for American producers. In June 2026, President Trump signed an Executive Order accelerating American agriculture innovation, empowering farmers and ranchers, and bolstering the strength and security of our food supply. In June 2026, President Trump safeguarded America’s food supply and supported domestic agricultural production by authorizing the temporary suspension of certain duties on phosphate fertilizer imported from Morocco, helping ensure an adequate supply of phosphate fertilizer for American Farmers. In June 2026, the Department of Agriculture announced the $500 million Fertilizer Investment & Expansion for Long Term Domestic Supply Program, to onshore domestic fertilizer production and lower prices for America’s farmers and ranchers. In August 2026, the Department of Agriculture and the Department of Health and Human Services announced the Harvest to Hallways initiative to put more American-raised beef and local products into school meals. The Administration remains engaged with the Hill on a Farm Bill to increase loan limits for Department of Agriculture guaranteed operating loans and farm ownership loans.

title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Promotes Fair Competition in Livestock Markets and Expands Market Access for American Meat Producers
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Promotes Fair Competition in Livestock Markets and Expands Market Access for American Meat Producers The White House September 4, 2026 ADVANCING COMPETITION AND ACCOUNTABILITY: Today, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order to support American producers’ ability to butcher, process, package, and sell their meat to consumers across state lines while maintaining the highest standards of food safety while avoiding being overcharged by monopolistic practices in the meat processing industry. The Order directs the Secretary of Agriculture to prioritize investigations into potential violations of the Packers and Stockyards Act, increase federal resources for these investigations, and review existing policies under the Act to strengthen protections for producers and ensure effective deterrence. The Order directs the Secretary of Agriculture to modernize meat inspections to focus on core safety, boost processing efficiency and technology, lower costs to add value for ranchers and consumers, and remove unnecessary and burdensome requirements that do not support essential food safety needs. The Order directs the Secretary of Agriculture to create a “one stop shop” resource and coordinator position within the Department of Agriculture to expand federal licensing and connect producers to inspection options, provide additional resources and training for small and very small meat processors, expand interstate market access for eligible meat products, and streamline processes to increase State participation in the State Meat and Poultry Inspection Program, the Cooperative Interstate Shipment Program, and the Talmadge-Aiken Cooperative Inspection Program. The Order directs the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a “Strengthening Processing for U.S. Ranchers” loan program to help small and regional processors continue their operations, expand their footprint, and increase diversity of animal proteins being processed. EXPANDING MARKET ACCESS FOR U.S. MEAT PRODUCTS: To strengthen the national food supply chain and foster competition, the Administration is expanding domestic market access for U.S. ranchers while maintaining food safety protections. Record-low beef herd size from the Biden Administration’s war on cattle that pursued radical climate activists’ misguided policies has strained America’s slaughter and processing infrastructure. President Trump is committed to promoting fair competition in livestock and meat markets, protecting producers and small processors from unfair, deceptive, or monopolistic practices, and expanding legitimate market opportunities for American-raised livestock and meat products. State-inspected small processors are currently unable to sell their products outside of their own state without heavy regulatory approval. This action ensures greater interstate market access for eligible meat products while maintaining the highest standards of food safety that help make U.S. born, raised, harvested, and processed food the best in the world. As Americans eat more beef than ever, increasing competition in the marketplace and sustaining processing capacity for ranchers is essential, particularly in light of consolidation in the processing industry and reduced capacity and options for ranchers. Over 40 years ago, the four largest beef packers accounted for 36 percent of all purchases of steers and heifers. Today, that has increased to 85 percent. The United States is the world’s largest consumer of beef by volume and ranks second globally in per capita beef consumption, underscoring beef’s importance to the American diet. As Americans eat more beef than ever, it is necessary and appropriate to ensure that the supply of beef products will be sufficient to meet U.S. demand at affordable and reasonable prices. Small and very small processors deserve unique focus, which is recognized by the work of the USDA Small Processors Action Plan, funding to reduce the costs of inspection, and the SPUR program. Strong slaughter and processing food‑safety standards preserve America’s reputation for world‑leading food quality. The Trump Administration has advanced this effort by establishing new federal–state cooperative agreements, such as in Georgia, and increasing state reimbursements—strengthening food safety while expanding market opportunities for ranchers, including sales across states lines. FIGHTING FOR AMERICA’S RANCHERS: Since Day One, President Trump and his Administration have worked and delivered for America’s ranchers and farmers – the backbone of our Nation’s economy and food supply. The Department of Agriculture expanded its Remote Grading Pilot Program to total 92 facilities in 34 States, helping many small- or mid-sized processors access official grading. President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts put more money in ranchers’ pockets each year, made the industry more attractive for investment, and boosted profitability for ranchers now and into the future. In October 2025, the Trump Administration announced new actions to fortify the American beef industry, reinforcing and prioritizing the American rancher’s critical role in the national security of the United States. Earlier this week, the Department of Agriculture announced its Ranchers First Initiative , building off of these actions to rebuild the great American beef industry, including revitalizing regional processing. In December 2025, President Trump signed an Executive Order to stop price fixing, anti-competitive behavior, and foreign influence that drives up grocery prices and threatens the security of America’s food supply. In January 2026, the Department of Agriculture launched its new “Product of the USA” label for meat, poultry, and eggs that are born, raised, harvested, and processed all in the United States to ensure marketing protection and benefits for American producers. In March 2026, the Department of Agriculture provided $20 million in reduced overtime and holiday inspection fees for small processors. In June 2026, the Department of Agriculture launched the Small Processors Action Plan and opened a fourth round of the Meat and Poultry Processing Expansion Program with $60 million to expand American processing capacity.

title: Presidential Message on National Recovery Month
text: Briefings & Statements Presidential Message on National Recovery Month The White House September 2, 2026 During National Recovery Month, we celebrate the more than 23 million Americans who have found a pathway from addiction to recovery, we recognize those who have helped them reclaim their lives, and we renew our commitment to supporting those still struggling to find hope and healing. Throughout every community in America, the effects of drug and alcohol addiction are felt in the lives of families, friends, and neighbors. Today, 48.4 million Americans suffer from addiction, and 69,973 Americans died last year to overdose. Every American deserves to live free from the grip of addiction—and my Administration is wholly committed to making that possible by preventing drug use before it starts, providing treatment at the earliest opportunity, and helping more Americans lead engaged and productive lives in recovery. In January, I was proud to establish the Great American Recovery Initiative, coordinating a national response to the disease of addiction across government, healthcare, faith communities, and the private sector while fostering a culture that celebrates recovery. I also signed an Executive Order on Ending Crime and Disorder on America’s Streets to make our communities safer and help homeless Americans access addiction and mental health services needed to rebuild their lives. I am directing the Food and Drug Administration to prioritize non-opioid options for chronic pain, and I signed the SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Reauthorization Act to strengthen federal grant programs for treatment, overdose response, and mental health care. We are also stopping deadly drugs before they ever reach our shores. I signed the HALT Fentanyl Act into law, classifying all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I drugs; formally designated major international drug cartels as foreign terrorist organizations; sealed our border; and empowered our brave Border Patrol and Armed Forces with the resources needed to carry out massive drug seizures to keep fentanyl off our streets. Recovery is a testament to the strength of the American Spirit and the promise of a second chance. This month, we stand with those on the road to recovery and the families and communities who support them along the way. Together, we will help more Americans break free from addiction and lead healthy, productive, and fulfilling lives.

title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Announces Historic Oil Agreement to Secure American Energy Dominance and Drive Venezuela’s Economic Recovery
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Announces Historic Oil Agreement to Secure American Energy Dominance and Drive Venezuela’s Economic Recovery The White House August 31, 2026 SECURING STABLE & LOW-COST OIL SUPPLY IN OUR HEMISPHERE: In the biggest oil deal in world history, President Donald J. Trump has secured U.S. majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves in Venezuela – vastly expanding our current U.S. territorial proven reserves of roughly 46 billion barrels. This deal secures our energy dominance for the next century—all at zero cost to the United States. The deal, signed by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, gives the U.S. government powerful governance rights, economic ownership, and guaranteed low-cost off-take from a new private Venezuelan oil champion, which will be the second-largest private oil company by reserves in the world: In connection with this agreement, the Venezuelan interim authorities have granted North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP), a privately held oil company that is the second-largest private Venezuelan oil producer and a proven operator, 100-year concessions for 17 oil fields with proven reserves of approximately 65 billion barrels. At no cost to the American taxpayer, NABEP has granted the U.S. Department of War’s Office of Strategic Capital a 35% equity stake in its corporate parent, representing up to hundreds of billions in value and dividends for the United States. NABEP has granted the U.S. Department of State the right to purchase, at production cost, a guaranteed 20% of the off-take from all current and future fields NABEP will operate—ensuring a stable supply of low-cost oil that can facilitate refilling the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR), which Joe Biden depleted to historic lows, and to provide supply for military and other sensitive uses. NABEP has also granted the U.S. Department of State the right of first refusal to purchase the remaining 80% of its production, providing a guaranteed source of energy in our hemisphere in emergency situations. The U.S. government has a veto power over the appointment of any member of the board of directors, and a majority of NABEP’s board of directors must be U.S. citizens. NABEP will have reputable U.S. auditors, lawyers, and advisors and the U.S. government’s agreement with NABEP is governed by U.S. law and is subject to the jurisdiction of U.S. courts. Millions of barrels of new Venezuelan output will be processed through U.S. refineries and pumped with American rigs and infrastructure, supporting billions in investment in the United States and thousands of jobs here at home. DRIVING ECONOMIC RECOVERY & THE RECONSTRUCTION OF VENEZUELA’S OIL SECTOR: This groundbreaking privatization and investment in Venezuela’s energy sector is a key step in the Trump Administration’s three-part plan of stabilization, reconstruction and democratic transition. Private-sector led growth in production, output, and investment in Venezuela is a key precondition to driving continued reform and democratic transition following the incredible success of Operation Absolute Resolve: NABEP has developed an ambitious plan to rapidly scale production by investing up to $100 billion in new oil infrastructure in Venezuela, helping to drive economic growth, support thousands of high-paying jobs in Venezuela, and lead to tens of billions in broader economic activity. NABEP’s concessions are governed by Venezuela’s new hydrocarbons law, adopted with U.S. support, which provides for historic modernization, privatization and development of Venezuela’s lagging oil sector. Under this framework, as it scales production, NABEP will pay an expected $200 billion in royalty and tax payments over the first 25 years, representing critical revenue and fiscal support for current and future Venezuelan governments to fund reconstruction and social development. After years of underinvestment and mismanagement, the majority of Venezuela’s oil fields are not producing or vastly underproducing. By investing in a proven private operator with a track record of scaling production in the country, who will be able to raise private American capital to fund capital expenditures, Venezuela has a historic opportunity to revitalize its key sector, drive oil output growth, and grow its economy. The U.S. government’s robust governance and audit provisions, along with the Trump Administration’s banking reform, payment oversight and financial monitorship, will ensure tax and royalty payments are spent in the interests of the Venezuelan people. The United States is sponsoring reconciliation talks between the 2015 National Assembly and the interim authorities – a process which has already resulted in significant reforms to the Venezuelan judiciary, the release of hundreds of political prisoners, and cooperative efforts to finance reconstruction following the devastating June earthquakes. The process will continue with additional meetings in September. REASSERTING THE MONROE DOCTRINE & EXPELLING FOREIGN ADVERSARIES FROM OUR HEMISPHERE: The majority of the incremental oil fields to be operated by NABEP were previously controlled or operated by Russian and Chinese firms, or by corrupt cronies of Maduro and Chavez. These malign foreign actors looted Venezuela’s resources for the benefit of American adversaries like Cuba, Russia and China and failed to invest in Venezuela’s infrastructure or development. President Trump has re-established the Monroe Doctrine, purging foreign malign influence from our backyard and ensuring American dominance in our hemisphere is never again questioned.
